items.name: Driver hours-of-service (HOS)
items.version: US: 49 CFR Part 395 (FMCSA); EU: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006
items.scope: Limits on commercial driver on-duty/driving time and mandatory rest breaks; typically enforced via an electronic logging device (ELD) in the US.
items.notes: Applies mainly to commercial motor vehicles above regulatory weight/passenger thresholds; exact thresholds and rest-break rules differ by jurisdiction and are flagged, not implemented, here. Neither cloned source (karrio, fleetbase) implements HOS logic; this entry is domain knowledge, not a claim that either product is compliant.

provenance.notes: fleetbase models driver time_window_start/end and schedule_constraints, which HOS compliance would build on, but does not implement HOS rules itself. Reasoned applicability.

items.name: Dangerous goods (hazmat) shipping
items.version: Road: ADR 2025 (UNECE ECE/TRANS/352), in force 1 Jan 2025; Air: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations (DGR), 67th Edition, effective 1 Jan 2026; Sea: IMDG Code 2024 Edition, Amendment 42-24, mandatory from 1 Jan 2026
items.jurisdiction: ADR: Europe and UNECE contracting parties (road, 53 countries); IATA DGR: global (air, contractual via IATA member airlines); IMDG Code: global (sea, IMO member states via SOLAS/MARPOL)
items.scope: Classification, labeling, packaging, and documentation requirements for shipments containing hazardous materials.
items.notes: Neither cloned source (karrio, fleetbase) models a dangerous-goods classification field. All three regimes require classification (UN number/class), packaging, marking/labelling, and shipping documentation for regulated materials; specifics differ by mode and are flagged for human review, not implemented here. Citing these standards is not a claim that any product is DG-compliant.

provenance.notes: All three editions/versions independently verified via their publishing bodies' own pages (UNECE, IATA, IMO) in this pass; this confirms the regulations and their current versions exist and apply to road/air/sea dangerous-goods transport respectively, not that any implementation satisfies them.

items.name: Customs and import/export regulations
items.version: Varies by jurisdiction (e.g. US CBP, EU Union Customs Code), harmonized at the data-element level by the WCO Data Model 4.3.0; responsibility/cost allocation standardized by Incoterms 2020 (ICC)
items.jurisdiction: Destination and origin country of an international shipment
items.scope: Declaration of contents, value, and origin for cross-border shipments; duties and taxes calculation.
items.notes: Flagged per the brief's guidance that customs is jurisdiction-specific and requires human review. The WCO Data Model standardizes the data elements customs administrations exchange, and Incoterms 2020 standardizes who is responsible for duties/customs at each stage of a shipment; neither, nor citing them here, is a claim that any implementation is customs-compliant in any specific jurisdiction.

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.customs embedded field is the direct implementation evidence; the WCO Data Model and Incoterms 2020 are authoritative, independently verified standards for the data-modeling and responsibility-allocation dimensions respectively. Enforcement specifics still vary per destination/origin jurisdiction and require human review.
